strings.name: Richie McCaw
strings.role: Rugby player · Two-time World Cup-winning captain
strings.summary: An openside flanker known for breakdown work, coverage and judgment, McCaw captained the All Blacks in 110 of his 148 Tests and led them to the 2011 and 2015 World Cups. A three-time world player of the year, he represented Canterbury and the Crusaders. After retiring in 2015, he pursued helicopter flying and adventure racing; a 2026 interview discussed designing a future GODZONE course.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Led New Zealand to World Cup titles and established a benchmark for leadership and performance in modern rugby.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Born in Oamaru, New Zealand, and raised in the Hakataramea area.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Consecutive World Cups
strings.highlights.h1.text: Captained the winning teams in 2011 and 2015.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Attended Otago Boys' High School, then Lincoln University, developing in Canterbury rugby.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Three world player awards
strings.highlights.h2.text: Named world player of the year in 2006, 2009 and 2010.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Discusses adventure-race design
strings.timeline.t1.text: Described moving from GODZONE competitor to course designer; the 2027 route remained in preparation.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Order of New Zealand
strings.timeline.t2.text: Received one of New Zealand's highest national honors in Wellington.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Announces retirement
strings.timeline.t4.title: World Cup retained
strings.timeline.t4.text: Led the All Blacks to victory over Australia in the London final.
strings.timeline.t5.title: First World Cup title
strings.timeline.t5.text: Defeated France in the Auckland final for a home victory.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Permanent captaincy
strings.timeline.t6.text: Became the All Blacks' main captain, beginning sustained leadership.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Test debut
strings.timeline.t7.text: Played Ireland in Dublin and was named player of the match.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Canterbury beginnings
strings.timeline.t8.text: Began provincial rugby before joining the Crusaders and national side the next year.
